# Svelte 5 Support is officially here!

After a way too long wait, which I (@jonasgeiler) really apologize for, I have finally managed to get back to this project and finalize a few last things for the full `v4` release. I have noticed that many people were already using the `next` tag on NPM anyways.

## About
Since [version `4.0.0-rc.2`](https://github.com/jonasgeiler/svelte-tiny-virtual-list/releases/tag/v4.0.0-rc.2) I have mainly added some bug fixes, both contributed by users and some that I have found. Apart from that, I have made some behind-the-scenes changes that should help with futu

open_gaps.why: we do runtime dynamic measurement instead of an upfront size map
virtua stabilized CacheSnapshot 2026-08-20; we restore scroll by index/offset but not measured sizes, so a deep restore re-measures
open_gaps.worth_doing: low urgency; only matters for lists restored deep into long dynamic-height datasets

open_gaps.gap: user-gesture takeover of an in-flight programmatic scroll / public cancelScroll()
open_gaps.why: keyboard input aborts our in-flight scroll(); wheel/touch takeover not verified and there is no public cancel API; 3.19.1 (2026-10-12) lets a user scroll end a non-smooth scrollToIndex before reconcile; 3.19.5 (2026-10-15) extends this to iOS 27 flings: a command during a fling stops it, user takeover cancels it; 3.19.7 (2026-10-22): explicit scroll cancels stale anchor work, clamped compensation retry held while a touch owns the scroll; 3.19.9 (2026-10-29): a command during a touch fling stops it on Android too
open_gaps.worth_doing: verify wheel/touch takeover first; public cancel is cheap if requested

open_gaps.why: Grouped lists can retain section headers while ordinary offscreen rows unmount; SvelteVirtualListProps has no sticky-row or keep-mounted API.
open_gaps.worth_doing: Evaluate only with a concrete grouped-list use case; no implementation commitment.

closed_gaps.gap: end-anchored scroll compensation recovery when the browser clamps the write
closed_gaps.why: resizeItem writes scrollTop before the new total size is committed; browser clamps to the old scroll max and the bottom pin is lost with no scroll event to correct it. We use the same compensation pattern with dynamic measurement. 3.17.10 (2026-09-11) also keeps an end-pinned list following appends when older items are trimmed in the same update with no count increase, and preserves reading anchors for users scrolled away from the end. 3.17.11 (2026-09-14) skips the prepend anchor scrollTop sync while a smooth programmatic scrollToIndex is in flight (an instant write cancels the smooth animation and Chromium drops a re-issued smooth request), and the debounced scroll-end fallback reads the live scroll offset instead of stale state.
closed_gaps.resolution: Covered by tests/other/scroll-compensation.spec.ts (8 probes, chromium+firefox+webkit). Clamped end-pin writes and smooth scroll() during measurement were already handled and are now regression-tested. Keyed mutations were the real gap: reconcileItemKeys never compensated scroll, so a keyed prepend or front trim moved the reading position by the full height of the changed rows (1979-2000px in the fixture) and an end-pinned list stopped following on append+trim (735px). Fixed by anchoring on the item key before the DOM updates.
